answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a refundable deposit that only unlocks after sustained useful work, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Reputation then accrues like cargo passing through a wharf: every verified delivery adds a small, time-decaying trust score, and a violet flag marks accounts whose behavior breaks the pattern. If one identity tries to spin up many clones, the spiral of rising stake costs and falling trust makes the attack unprofitable before it can distort prices.
